title: Environment, motion and instrument monitoring
text: **S31 · Environmental monitoring candidate · Resistance thermometry**

pages.title: S31 Resistance temperature measurement
text: **S31 · Environmental monitoring candidate · Resistance thermometry**

Resistance temperature measurement uses a material’s predictable resistance-temperature relationship. The complete result depends on the sensor, excitation, wiring, reference and conversion model. Four-wire arrangements can reduce lead-resistance effects, but they do not remove self-heating, placement or calibration uncertainty. [R20]
## Signal and useful question

The instrument measures resistance in ohms and derives temperature in degrees Celsius or kelvin. Useful questions include whether the relevant observation environment is stable, whether electronics are overheating and whether a process experienced an excursion.
## Location defines meaning

A sensor attached to a wall measures a different thermal environment from a sensor near the plate or on a processor. The record should identify location and mounting, and any inference about the sample temperature should be supported by a transfer study.

For Reader V1, temperature monitoring can support instrument characterization and fault detection. Integrated incubation would require a broader spatial and temporal assessment. Multiple agreeing sensors do not demonstrate uniformity if they are all placed in the same unrepresentative region. Qualification should include the conditions and positions that could reveal a meaningful gradient.
tables: Traceable temperature references across the intended range and complete signal-chain verification.
Self-heating, lead mismatch, thermal contact, response lag, gradients and electrical noise.
Suitable placement, wiring, analog measurement and protection from damage or contamination.
Temperature uncertainty and response time appropriate to the monitored location.

pages.title: S32 Capacitive relative humidity sensing
text: **S32 · Environmental monitoring candidate · Capacitive humidity measurement**

A capacitive humidity sensor uses a material whose dielectric response changes with water vapour exposure. The instrument converts that response into relative humidity through calibration and compensation. Relative humidity depends on temperature and describes a local gas condition, not the total water content of a plate.
## Signal and useful question

The derived output is relative humidity in percent, accompanied by temperature and sensor quality status. Candidate uses include detecting environmental changes that may affect condensation, evaporation or instrument reliability.
## Condensation is a separate event

A high humidity reading does not establish that droplets are present on the optical path, and a local sensor may miss condensation elsewhere. Image-based obstruction checks and environmental monitoring can complement each other, but they answer different questions.

The proposed system should retain sensor saturation or recovery states rather than displaying an apparently precise value throughout a compromised interval. If humidity is used in a biological model, the analysis should account for the sensor’s location and lag. Its most defensible initial role is environmental context and instrument quality assessment, with any growth-related inference evaluated separately.
tables: Suitable humidity references, temperature dependence and response-time checks.
Condensation, chemical exposure, contamination, hysteresis, placement and slow recovery after saturation.
Representative airflow, protection that does not create excessive lag and a serviceable mounting.
Stable local measurement under the intended humidity and contamination conditions.

pages.title: S33 Pressure measurement
text: **S33 · Environmental and control candidate · Pressure measurement**

Pressure sensors convert mechanical deformation or another pressure-dependent effect into an electrical signal. Absolute, gauge and differential measurements use different reference conditions. A value without its reference type can be misleading even when its numerical units are correct.
## Signal and useful question

The output is pressure in pascals or a declared multiple. Candidate functions include monitoring a gas path, detecting an obstruction or assessing a pressure difference across a relevant assembly. The selected function determines the required range, response time and reference.
## Pressure alone does not prove containment

A pressure difference can support an engineering assessment, but it does not independently establish airflow direction everywhere, filter integrity or biological containment. Those claims require the relevant system-level evaluation.

The instrument should distinguish a measured process change from a failed sensor line. Plausibility checks, maintenance records and independent observations can help resolve that difference. If a pressure measurement is required for a control decision, the response to unavailable or implausible data should be specified before the control function is enabled. The initial catalogue role is engineering monitoring rather than a direct biological measurement.
tables: Traceable pressure reference, zero, span, temperature behaviour and line integrity.
Leaks, blocked tubing, condensate, offset drift, mounting stress and pressure-port placement.
Compatible ports, tubing, seals, protective interfaces and accessible maintenance.
Reliable detection of the intended condition with a defined fault response.

pages.title: S34 Airflow measurement
text: **S34 · Environmental and control candidate · Flow measurement**

Airflow can be measured through several physical approaches, including thermal transfer and pressure-related methods. Each responds to a defined flow path and fluid condition. A local reading should not be assumed to describe circulation throughout an enclosure.
## Signal and useful question

Outputs may be volumetric flow in litres per minute, mass flow or local velocity in metres per second. Temperature, pressure and gas composition may be needed to interpret or convert the quantity. Candidate uses include monitoring cooling, detecting a restricted path or characterizing a research gas-sampling arrangement.
## Connect flow to the consequence

The product should identify why the measurement matters. Reduced electronics cooling may require throttling or shutdown. A changed research sampling flow may invalidate the time relationship between a plate and a gas observation. Those responses have different priorities and should not share an unexplained generic alarm.

Flow measurement is a proposed engineering channel. Its presence does not establish sterile airflow or safe containment. Qualification should evaluate the complete path and the relevant failure modes, including disconnected tubing or a sensor that reports plausible flow while the intended sampling route is bypassed.
tables: Suitable flow reference, gas conditions, path geometry and response across the intended range.
Leaks, turbulence, fouling, gas composition, temperature and flow-profile changes.
Defined duct or channel, low unwanted restriction and service access.
A flow quantity relevant to the function and robust to expected path changes.

pages.title: S35 Strain gauge weighing
text: **S35 · Mechanical monitoring candidate · Gravimetric measurement**

Strain-gauge weighing measures deformation of a load-bearing element and converts it to force or mass under a calibrated model. A plate assembly includes the vessel, medium, water and any biological material. Changes in those contributions are not automatically separable.
## Signal and useful question

The primary electrical response is a bridge signal, with derived load in newtons or mass in grams. Candidate functions include plate presence, gross fill checks, evaporation research and mechanical monitoring. A whole-plate mass change should not be labelled microbial biomass without a separately established relationship.
## Compare signal size with the disturbance

Nominal converter resolution is not the same as usable mass resolution. An instrument may display many decimal places while drift and handling variation dominate the change of interest. The evaluation should report repeatability and stability over the intended observation interval.

The proposed initial role is engineering and research context. Presence detection or evaporation tracking may be useful without making any biological inference. If mass data are included in fusion, preserve taring events and mechanical configuration changes so that an apparent discontinuity is not interpreted as a sudden biological event.
tables: Traceable masses, zero, span, loading position, hysteresis and drift.
Evaporation, condensation, handling forces, thermal drift, cable forces and mechanical creep.
Stable support, isolation from motion and a reproducible load path.
Useful change resolution under actual environmental and mechanical conditions.

pages.title: S36 Optical distance and presence sensing
text: **S36 · Instrument-control candidate · Optical ranging and presence**

Optical distance sensing estimates range through time-of-flight, triangulation or another declared optical principle. A coarse multizone sensor can support presence, position or clearance checks. Its spatial sampling and ranging uncertainty should not be confused with microscopic three-dimensional imaging. Manufacturer multizone ranging documentation supports an engineering presence use, not colony topography. [R19]
## Signal and useful question

Outputs include distance in millimetres, return strength and measurement-validity indicators. Candidate functions include checking that a plate or mechanism occupies a permitted region and detecting gross deviations before capture or motion.
## Use validity information

A numerical range can be unreliable when the return signal is weak or when several surfaces contribute. The control interface should preserve validity flags and avoid converting an invalid range into a confident “plate present” state.

This candidate supports instrument readiness and motion checks. If finer shape information is needed for research, a separately qualified optical method should be considered. The proposed evaluation should challenge the sensor with empty holders, permitted vessels, misalignment and reflective or transparent surfaces, then verify that the system responds appropriately when distance is unavailable or ambiguous.
tables: Known distances, target materials, ambient-light conditions and alignment.
Transparent surfaces, multiple reflections, low return signal, contamination and object angle.
Clear optical path, mounting stability and quality-aware control logic.
Reliable detection of the intended mechanical state under permitted target conditions.

pages.title: S37 Magnetic position encoding
text: **S37 · Instrument-control candidate · Magnetic position measurement**

Magnetic position encoders infer displacement or rotation from a magnetic field and its relationship to a sensing element. They can provide feedback without an exposed optical scale. Their performance depends on magnet geometry, alignment, field conditions and the conversion model.
## Signal and useful question

Outputs include angle in degrees or radians, position in length units and status information. Candidate functions include verifying mechanism position, indexing a plate holder or detecting whether a shutter has reached a permitted state.
## Measure the mechanism rather than only the motor

An encoder on a motor shaft may report commanded rotation while a coupling slips or a downstream mechanism remains displaced. The relevant feedback location should follow the physical state that the system needs to know.

This is a proposed control-sensing option, not a biological modality. Qualification should include plausible failures such as misalignment, lost feedback or mechanical play. The software should distinguish estimated, commanded and confirmed positions. A safety-relevant action should not proceed merely because the last remembered position was acceptable before a restart or service intervention.
tables: Known positions, magnet alignment, full travel behaviour and repeatability.
External magnetic fields, temperature, magnet variation, mechanical backlash and mounting shifts.
Stable magnet-sensor geometry, control interface and independent limit or interlock strategy where required.
Feedback accuracy and fault detectability appropriate to the controlled mechanism.

pages.title: S38 Inertial vibration measurement
text: **S38 · Instrument-monitoring candidate · Inertial measurement**

An accelerometer measures specific force along defined axes; related inertial sensors may measure angular motion. These channels can help characterize vibration, handling shocks and movement during acquisition. Their output depends on mounting, bandwidth, orientation and the influence of gravity.
## Signal and useful question

Acceleration is expressed in metres per second squared or in a declared multiple of standard gravity. Frequency-domain descriptors can summarize vibration over an observation interval. The useful question is whether mechanical disturbance is large enough to compromise the selected image or instrument state.
## Link vibration to an optical consequence

A vibration signal should not trigger an arbitrary rejection threshold without evidence. The qualification should compare inertial observations with image blur, registration error or another relevant outcome. Some measured vibration may be harmless, while an unmonitored local motion may still affect the optics.

This channel is proposed for engineering characterization and readiness checks. It may also help investigate transport damage or recurring faults. The record should preserve the interval and bandwidth used for a summary, because a single “vibration score” can conceal whether a short shock occurred during the actual exposure or at an irrelevant time.
tables: Axis scale, offset, alignment, frequency response and timestamp accuracy.
Mounting resonance, temperature, aliasing, gravity projection and electrical noise.
Rigid representative placement, synchronized sampling and signal processing.
Demonstrated relationship between the monitored disturbance and measurement quality.

pages.title: S39 Electrical power monitoring
text: **S39 · Instrument-monitoring candidate · Electrical power measurement**

Voltage and current monitoring can reveal supply instability, overload, abnormal consumption or a failing subsystem. Electrical power is derived from the appropriate voltage-current relationship, with waveform and measurement timing considered where relevant. A low reported average can conceal short disturbances that affect capture or storage.
## Signal and useful question

Outputs include volts, amperes, watts and integrated energy in joules or watt-hours. Candidate functions include detecting undervoltage, verifying a load budget and relating faults to acquisition or processing activity.
## Preserve the affected operation

A power fault during storage may threaten record completeness, while a disturbance during exposure may alter an image. The system should associate the event with the relevant operation and verify recovery rather than merely clearing an alarm after the voltage returns.

This proposed channel supports reliability and service. It does not measure biological activity. Qualification should include controlled electrical load scenarios, safe shutdown and restart behaviour, and verification that a partial record cannot appear complete. Power monitoring is especially useful when paired with data-integrity checks that reveal whether an electrical event had a lasting consequence.
tables: Reference voltage and current, sense-path resistance, offset and sampling response.
Transients, wiring drops, thermal drift, measurement bandwidth and shared ground effects.
Appropriate sensing location, protection, isolation where needed and event synchronization.
Detection of disturbances that can affect the actual instrument function.

pages.title: S40 Reference photodiode monitoring
text: **S40 · Instrument-monitoring candidate · Optical reference measurement**

A reference photodiode measures light at a defined location in the illumination path. With a suitable response calibration, it can help distinguish a changing source from a changing sample. Its observation is local and spectrally weighted by the detector response.
## Signal and useful question

The primary quantity is photocurrent or converted voltage. Derived optical power or relative intensity requires a stated responsivity and geometry. Candidate uses include monitoring source stability, detecting a failed illumination channel and verifying exposure synchronization.
## A source check is not a full-field check

The photodiode may report stable light while a diffuser shifts, a lens becomes contaminated or one part of the field darkens. It should complement, rather than replace, spatial image-quality verification. A reference channel also shares some failure mechanisms with the source it monitors, so independent checks remain useful.

This candidate is particularly relevant to a controlled imaging reader. The proposed evaluation should determine which faults the reference can detect, how quickly it detects them and which faults remain invisible. The result should be a specific quality-control function with an explicit limit, not a general assurance that every captured image is correctly illuminated.
tables: Detector responsivity, linearity, dark offset, amplifier gain and reference geometry.
Detector ageing, temperature, contamination, stray light and spectral mismatch with the imaging path.
A representative pick-off location, stable optics and synchronized acquisition.
Reliable detection of illumination changes relevant to image quality.
